metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Kazakhstan

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for Kazakhstan using OECD’s published PISA 2022 database tables rather than presenting a new student-level re-analysis. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD’s database tables are produced using PISA’s complex survey methodology and associated sampling weights (and replicate procedures where applicable) to obtain population-representative estimates and correct uncertainty. Because this document is a descriptive results factsheet, it does not specify the exact weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight method in the text provided. Analysts using the PISA 2022 database should apply the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights supplied with the dataset when reproducing estimates, and should use the OECD-provided PV/scaling outputs for creative thinking proficiency.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive OECD factsheet that reports already-scaled PISA 2022 creative thinking results from the OECD PISA 2022 database tables, rather than conducting an original empirical analysis that would require the authors to document PV combination or missing-data handling procedures. Plausible values and missing-data handling are handled within the OECD’s PISA scaling and database production pipeline, which is not detailed in this factsheet text. Therefore, the PV and missing-data handling strategies are not reported at the factsheet level.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports Kazakhstan results for 15-year-old students assessed in PISA 2022 creative thinking. It specifies that, in Kazakhstan, 19,769 students in 571 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science (representing about 272,400 15-year-olds), and that the creative thinking cognitive test was implemented in Kazakhstan as part of PISA 2022 Volume III. No additional analytic inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., item completion thresholds, missing-data exclusions) are described in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes creative thinking performance for Kazakhstan among 15-year-old students. PISA 2022 Creative Thinking is a cognitive test with 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating/improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Kazakhstan’s mean creative thinking score is 24 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average (33). The factsheet also reports proficiency distribution: 47% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline), and 12% are top performers at Levels 5–6. Within Kazakhstan, socio-economic status, gender, and students’ beliefs/attitudes are described as associated with creative thinking, and the document notes COVID-19-related implementation cautions for some countries/economies (asterisk conventions), though Kazakhstan’s specific caution status is not indicated in the provided excerpt.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD descriptive results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. It does not train or evaluate machine learning models, does not report an analytic ML pipeline, and does not provide student-level sampling/weight variable names or PV/missing-data handling procedures in the excerpt. Consequently, ML technique fields and structured predictive findings are intentionally left empty, while the outcome summary focuses on the reported PISA creative thinking benchmarks and descriptive relationships.
